title: The equations of a relative global complete intersection form a regular sequence at every prime
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $n,c\ge0$ integers, $P=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ the polynomial ring [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] and $f_1,\dots,f_c\in P$ such that $S=P/(f_1,\dots,f_c)$ is a relative global complete intersection over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection]. Let $\mathfrak q\subset S$ be a prime ideal and $\mathfrak q'\subset P$ its inverse image under the quotient map $P\to S$ (a prime ideal containing $f_1,\dots,f_c$), and let $P_{\mathfrak q'}$ be the localization of $P$ at $\mathfrak q'$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Then $f_1/1,\dots,f_c/1$ is a regular sequence in the local ring $P_{\mathfrak q'}$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence].

proof.text: Use Noetherian approximation to obtain a finite type integer subring R0 and equations f0. Their coefficient equalities imply that the original equations are exactly the coefficientwise images of f0.

For any finite type integer subring B containing R0, equip B with the inclusion R0-algebra structure. Base change preserves the specified presentation. B is Noetherian. The contracted polynomial prime contains all mapped equations, since their composites to R[x] are the original equations.
Apply the proved Noetherian local regularity theorem at every contracted prime and retain its weak-regularity conclusion.
Apply finite coefficient-subring weak-regularity descent to obtain weak regularity in the original polynomial local ring.

The inverse image of q contains every equation. Its extension is the maximal ideal of its prime localization, so every displayed equation lies in this maximal ideal. The local finite-module regularity criterion converts weak regularity into regularity, including an empty sequence.
